verdict.rationale: Lium's billing docs state pods are billed per second (hourly price × seconds / 3600) with no minimum and no reservation. Pods can be auto-removed by TTL, end time or spend cap, which ties charges to the pod's lifetime. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that billing stops the moment a pod is removed (or of any stopped/paused state), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the per-second billing.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I am billed at per-second or per-minute granularity and only while my instance is actually running

citations.quote: You pay **per second**: `hourly price × seconds / 3600`, with no minimum.
Lium bills every GPU per second with no minimum and no reservation.
Pick one, and the pod is deleted when it is reached
